params.why: the slant height must be a whole number, so that the working stays clean

constraints: s * s == m * m + h * h
stem: A pyramid has a square base with sides of ${=b}$ cm. Its vertical height (from the apex straight down to the centre of the base) is ${=h}$ cm, and each of its four identical triangular faces has a slant height of ${=s}$ cm. What is the total surface area of the pyramid?
solution: The surface area is the area of the square base plus the area of the four triangular faces.

The height of each triangular face is the slant height, ${=s}$ cm, because it is measured along the face. The vertical height of ${=h}$ cm runs inside the pyramid and is not the height of a face, so it is not used here.
Area of the four faces: $4\times\frac{1}{2}\times{=b}\times{=s}={=2*b*s}\text{ cm}^{2}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Base left out of the total surface area
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student adds up only the four triangular faces and forgets the square base, so the answer is 2bh_s instead of b^2 + 2bh_s.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Triangle area without the one half
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student finds the area of each triangular face as base times slant height, leaving out the factor of one half, so the four faces come to 4bh_s instead of 2bh_s.

notes: Standard tier, built on the book's own decoy: ex13-4-4 and ex13-7-10 print the vertical height beside the slant height. Every instance satisfies h^2 + (b/2)^2 = s^2 (table of Pythagorean triples, 14 of them, so the printed vertical height is true for the printed slant height). Three distractors, each a named error; all four options are proved distinct for every table row (b+2h = 2s is impossible because (m+h)^2 > m^2+h^2). The mcq earns its place because each distractor is diagnosable, and the existing catalogue id is used on the vertical-height option.
